html:
Muhammad of Ghor was a sultan of the Ghurid dynasty from Ghor in central Afghanistan, whose conquests in north India from the 1170s to 1206 laid the base of the Delhi Sultanate. He ruled the eastern Ghurid lands from Ghazni while his elder brother ruled from Firozkoh, and became sole sultan in 1203.

His Indian campaigns:

  • 1175: took Multan.
  • 1178: beaten by the Chaulukya army of Gujarat at Kasahrada.
  • 1186: ended the last Ghaznavid rule, at Lahore.
  • 1191: beaten by Prithviraj Chauhan at the first battle of Tarain.
  • 1192: won the second battle of Tarain and took Ajmer and Delhi from the Chahamanas.
  • 1194: killed the Gahadavala king Jayachandra at Chandawar, opening the Ganges plain (see the late Pratiharas and their successors).

He left the running of India to his slave generals. In 1206, on his way back from putting down a revolt in the Punjab, he was murdered in his camp near the Jhelum. His general Qutb ud-Din Aibak then ruled at Delhi as the first sultan, and began the Qutb Minar.
